subject: math
title: Decimals to Hundredths: Compare, Order, Round and Multiply by 0.1
seo_title: Grade 5 Decimals to Hundredths Worksheets: Compare, Round, × 0.1 and × 0.01 (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Read, represent, compare, and order decimal numbers up to hundredths, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on decimals to hundredths for the Ontario curriculum: hundred grids, place value, comparing and ordering decimals, rounding to the nearest tenth, and multiplying by 0.1 and 0.01. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Tenths are the first place after the decimal point; hundredths are the second. 0.5 = 0.50 > 0.45.
key_sub: To round to the nearest tenth, look at the hundredths digit: 5 or more rounds up (2.47 → 2.5). × 0.1 is ÷ 10 and × 0.01 is ÷ 100, so 45 × 0.1 = 4.5 and 45 × 0.01 = 0.45.
body_html:
Tenths and hundredths

Split 1 whole into 100 equal parts. Each part is one hundredth: 1100 = 0.01. One column of 10 parts is one tenth: 110 = 0.1. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point, and hundredths go in the second place.

Place value

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. Use a 0 to hold an empty place: 7100 = 0.07.

Example 1

Write 8100 as a decimal.

8 hundredths. There are 0 tenths, so put a 0 in the tenths place.

Answer: 0.08

Comparing and ordering

Compare the whole numbers first, then the tenths, then the hundredths. It helps to give both numbers the same number of places: 0.5 = 0.50.

Example 2

Order 0.5, 0.45 and 0.4 from smallest to greatest.

Write them with hundredths: 0.50, 0.45, 0.40.

Answer: 0.4, 0.45, 0.5

Rounding to the nearest tenth

Find the two tenths the number is between. Look at the hundredths digit: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down.

Example 3

Round 3.96 to the nearest tenth.

3.96 is between 3.9 and 4.0. The hundredths digit is 6, so round up. 10 tenths make 1 whole.

Answer: 4.0

Multiplying by 0.1 and 0.01

× 0.1 is the same as ÷ 10: each digit moves one place to the right. × 0.01 is the same as ÷ 100: each digit moves two places to the right. Multiplying by 0.1 or 0.01 makes a number smaller.

Number× 0.1 (÷ 10)× 0.01 (÷ 100)
454.50.45
250252.5
80.80.08
Example 4

A dime is $0.10. How much are 46 dimes worth?

46 × 0.1 = 46 ÷ 10 = 4.6.

Answer: $4.60

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.45 > 0.5 because 45 > 5Use the same places: 0.45 < 0.50
Writing 7100 as 0.7Hundredths need two places: 0.07
Rounding 2.47 to 2.4 by dropping the 7Look at the hundredths digit: 7 rounds up to 2.5
Rounding to the wrong place: 8.75 → 9Nearest tenth keeps one decimal place: 8.8
45 × 0.1 = 450× 0.1 makes it smaller: 45 × 0.1 = 4.5

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about decimals in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 5 math curriculum, students read, represent, compare and order decimals to hundredths, round decimals to the nearest tenth, and multiply whole numbers by 0.1 and 0.01 using mental math.

faq.q: How do you round a decimal to the nearest tenth?
faq.a: Find the two tenths the number is between and look at the hundredths digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down, so 2.47 rounds to 2.5 and 6.13 rounds to 6.1.
The 5 in 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is 50 hundredths. 0.45 is only 45 hundredths, so 0.5 is bigger even though it has fewer digits.

faq.q: How do you multiply by 0.1 and 0.01 in your head?
faq.a: Multiplying by 0.1 is the same as dividing by 10, so each digit moves one place to the right: 45 × 0.1 = 4.5. Multiplying by 0.01 is the same as dividing by 100: 45 × 0.01 = 0.45.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 3 full columns and 4 squares are shaded: 3 tenths and 4 hundredths = 34100 = 0.34.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth. 7 full columns are shaded: 7 tenths = 710 = 0.7 (or 0.70). 0.07 would be only 7 small squares. 0.3 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each small square is 1 hundredth. 9 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 9 hundredths = 9100 = 0.09. Write a 0 in the tenths place. 0.91 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 8 full columns and 5 squares are shaded: 8 tenths and 5 hundredths = 85100 = 0.85. 0.15 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: One full grid is shaded: that is 1 whole. The second grid has 3 full columns and 6 squares: 36 hundredths. 1 and 36100 = 1.36. 0.36 forgets the whole grid.

items.q: Each grid is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Two full grids are shaded: 2 wholes. The third grid has only 5 squares: 5 hundredths. There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 2.05. 2.5 would be 2 and 5 tenths (50 squares).

items.q: 1 whole is split into 100 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: Each part is 1100 of the whole, one hundredth: 0.01. 0.1 is one tenth: 1 whole split into 10 parts.

items.q: How many hundredths make 1 tenth?
items.e: On a hundred grid, 1 column is 1 tenth and it has 10 small squares. So 10 hundredths = 1 tenth.

items.q: Write 27100 as a decimal.
items.e: 27100 is 27 hundredths: 2 tenths and 7 hundredths. The tenths digit is 2 and the hundredths digit is 7: 0.27.

items.q: Write 6100 as a decimal.
items.e: 6100 is 6 hundredths. Hundredths need two places after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.06. (0.6 would be 6 tenths.)

items.q: Write 3 45100 as a decimal.
items.e: 3 wholes, then the decimal point, then 45 hundredths (4 tenths and 5 hundredths): 3.45.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.08?
items.e: 0.08 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. The tenths digit is 0: 0.08 = 8 hundredths = 8100. (810 is 0.8.)

items.q: 0.4 is the same as how many hundredths?
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths. Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 40100. 4100 is only 0.04.

items.q: Which hundred grid shows 0.04?
items.e: 0.04 is 4 hundredths: only 4 small squares, with no full column. That is grid A. B shows 0.4, C shows 0.14 and D shows 0.44.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.3 to 0.4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth (0.01). The dot is 6 spaces after 0.30: 0.36.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: Each space from 1 to 2 is 0.1. The dot is halfway between 1.4 and 1.5. Halfway between 1.40 and 1.50 is 1.45.

items.q:
Count on in hundredths. What comes next?
2.97, 2.98, 2.99, ?
items.e: 2.99 + 0.01: 9 hundredths and 1 more make 10 hundredths, which is 1 more tenth. Then 10 tenths make 1 more whole. So the next number is 3.00 (the same as 3). There is no such step as 2.100.

items.q: 14 of this grid is shaded. Which decimal is equal to 14?
items.e: 14 of 100 squares is 25 squares. 25 squares = 25 hundredths = 0.25. 0.4 just copies the 4 from the fraction.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 25?
items.e: Make tenths: 25 = 410 (multiply the top and bottom by 2). 4 tenths = 0.4. 0.25 just writes the 2 and the 5 after the point.

items.q: Priya colours 38 squares of a hundred grid blue and 27 squares green. What decimal of the grid is not coloured?
items.e: 38 + 27 = 65 squares are coloured. 100 − 65 = 35 squares are not coloured: 0.35. 0.65 is the coloured part.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 4.36?
items.e: The red 3 is in the first place after the decimal point, in the tenths column. Its value is 3 tenths = 0.3.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 27.58?
items.e: The red 8 is in the second place after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 8 hundredths = 0.08.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 152.07?
items.e: The red 7 is in the second place after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 7 hundredths = 0.07. The 0 holds the tenths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 608.9?
items.e: The red 6 is three places before the decimal point, in the hundreds column. Its value is 6 hundreds = 600.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 5 in 3.45?
items.e: In 3.45 the 5 is in the hundredths place, the second place after the point. It is worth 0.05.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 18.6?
items.e: In 18.6 the 8 is in the ones place, just before the point. It is worth 8.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 240.9?
items.e: In 240.9 the 9 is in the tenths place, the first place after the point. It is worth 0.9.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 431.25?
items.e: In 431.25 the 4 is in the hundreds place (third place before the point). It is worth 400.

items.q: In 58.17, which digit is in the tenths place?
items.e: Read the places from the decimal point: tenths is the first digit after the point and hundredths is the second. In 58.17, the tenths digit is 1 and the hundredths digit is 7. The answer is 1.

items.q: In 906.34, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: Read the places from the decimal point: tenths is the first digit after the point and hundredths is the second. In 906.34, the tenths digit is 3 and the hundredths digit is 4. The answer is 4.
3 tens, 6 ones, 2 tenths and 5 hundredths: 3 6 . 2 5 = 36.25.
There are no tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 7 . 0 9 = 7.09. 7.9 would be 7 ones and 9 tenths.

items.q: Which shows 46.83 in expanded form?
items.e: 4 tens, 6 ones, 8 tenths and 3 hundredths: 40 + 6 + 0.8 + 0.03.

items.q: Which decimal is 5 tens, 2 ones and 4 hundredths?
items.e: 5 tens and 2 ones make 52. There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 before the 4 hundredths: 52.04.

items.q: Write nine and twelve hundredths as a decimal.
items.e: “Nine” is the whole number. “And” is the decimal point. Twelve hundredths = 0.12. So the number is 9.12.

items.q: How do you read 3.07?
items.e: 3 is the whole number. Say “and” for the decimal point. The 7 is in the hundredths place (0.07), so read it as three and seven hundredths.

items.q: How many hundredths are there in 0.8?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 8 tenths = 80 hundredths. 0.8 = 0.80.

items.q: How many tenths are there in 4.6?
items.e: 1 whole = 10 tenths, so 4 wholes = 40 tenths. 40 + 6 = 46 tenths. (6 is only the digit in the tenths place.)

items.q: 0.58 = 4 tenths and ? hundredths
items.e: Take 1 of the 5 tenths and rename it as 10 hundredths: 10 + 8 = 18. So 0.58 = 4 tenths and 18 hundredths (0.4 + 0.18 = 0.58).

items.q: How many hundredths are there in 1.24?
items.e: 1 whole = 100 hundredths. 100 + 24 = 124 hundredths. So 1.24 = 124100.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60. Both have 6 tenths. Compare the hundredths: 2 > 0. So 0.62 > 0.6.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.5 as 0.50 so both have hundredths. 50 hundredths > 45 hundredths, so 0.5 > 0.45. Do not compare 5 with 45: the 5 in 0.5 is 5 tenths.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Both have 3 ones. Compare the tenths: 3.08 has 0 tenths and 3.8 has 8 tenths. So 3.08 < 3.8.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the whole numbers first: 12 > 9. So 12.4 > 9.87, even though 9.87 has more digits.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 3 tenths = 30 hundredths. So 7.30 = 7.3.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.09 has 0 tenths and 0.1 has 1 tenth. So 0.09 < 0.1, even though 9 > 1.

items.q: Which number is greater than 0.7?
items.e: 0.7 = 0.70. 0.71 is 71 hundredths, which is more than 70 hundredths. So 0.71 > 0.7. 0.69 and 0.65 have only 6 tenths, and 0.07 has 0 tenths.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: All have 0 ones. Compare the tenths: 8, 7, 0 and 7. 0.8 has the most tenths, so it is the greatest, even though 0.79 has more digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.38 has 3 tenths and the others have 4, 8 and 5. So 0.38 is the smallest.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths = 60 hundredths = 0.60. A 0 at the end does not change the value. 0.06 is only 6 hundredths.

items.q: Which decimal is less than 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 = 0.30. 0.29 is 29 hundredths, less than 30 hundredths. So 0.29 < 0.3.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 0.4 = 0.40, and 40 hundredths > 38 hundredths. So 0.4 > 0.38 is true.

items.q: Which number is between 2.3 and 2.4?
items.e: 2.3 = 2.30 and 2.4 = 2.40. 2.35 is 2 and 35 hundredths, between 30 and 40 hundredths.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: 9.99 and 1.11 are less than 10. Compare 10.1 and 10.09: 1 tenth > 0 tenths. So 10.1 is the greatest.

items.q: Which letter shows 0.52?
items.e: Each space is 0.1. 0.52 is just after 0.5 (2 hundredths more). That is point C. B is 0.45, just before 0.5, and A is 0.25 (the digits of 0.52 swapped).

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.5, 0.45, 0.4
items.e: Write them with hundredths: 0.50, 0.45, 0.40. 40 < 45 < 50, so the order is 0.4, 0.45, 0.5. 0.45 is not the biggest just because it has more digits.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 3.2, 3.02, 3.12
items.e: All have 3 ones. Write them with hundredths: 3.20, 3.02, 3.12. 2 < 12 < 20 hundredths, so 3.02, 3.12, 3.2.

items.q: Order from greatest to smallest: 1.9, 1.09, 1.19, 0.99
items.e: 0.99 is less than 1, so it is the smallest. Write the others with hundredths: 1.90, 1.09, 1.19. Greatest first: 1.9, 1.19, 1.09, 0.99. Careful: the question asks for greatest first.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 5.6, 5.06, 6.5, 5.65
items.e: 6.5 has 6 ones, so it is the greatest. The others have 5 ones: 5.06, 5.60, 5.65. 6 < 60 < 65 hundredths, so the order is 5.06, 5.6, 5.65, 6.5.

items.q:
Which digit can go in the box to make this true?
0.4□ < 0.43
items.e: Both numbers have 4 tenths, so compare the hundredths. The hundredths digit must be less than 3: 0.42 < 0.43. So 2 works. With 3 the numbers are equal, and 5 or 9 make it greater.

sets.title: Round decimals to the nearest tenth

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (2.47) to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 2.47 is between 2.4 and 2.5. Look at the hundredths digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up to 2.5. The dot is closer to 2.5 than to 2.4.

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (6.13) to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 6.13 is between 6.1 and 6.2. Look at the hundredths digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down to 6.1. The dot is closer to 6.1.

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (0.85) to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 0.85 is between 0.8 and 0.9. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 0.9. 0.85 is exactly halfway. When the hundredths digit is 5, round up. 0.85 is not rounded yet: a number of tenths has only one decimal place.

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (3.96) to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 3.96 is between 3.9 and 4.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 4.0. The tenths digit is 9, so 1 more tenth makes 10 tenths: that is 1 more whole. The answer 4.0 shows it is rounded to tenths. 3.10 is wrong: 10 tenths are not written in one place.

items.q: Round 5.32 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 5.32 is between 5.3 and 5.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 2. 4 or less, so round down to 5.3. 5.4 rounds the wrong way, and 5 rounds to the nearest whole number.

items.q: Round 8.75 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 8.75 is between 8.7 and 8.8. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 8.8. 9 rounds to the nearest whole number instead of the nearest tenth.

items.q: Round 0.64 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 0.64 is between 0.6 and 0.7. Look at the hundredths digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 0.6. 0.7 rounds the wrong way. 0 and 1 are whole numbers, not tenths.

items.q: Round 12.08 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 12.08 is between 12.0 and 12.1. Look at the hundredths digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 12.1. 12.0 just drops the 8. 12.8 moves the 8 into the tenths place.

items.q: Round 1.98 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 1.98 is between 1.9 and 2.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up to 2.0. The tenths digit is 9, so 1 more tenth makes 10 tenths: that is 1 more whole. The answer is written 2.0 to show tenths. 1.9 just drops the 8.

items.q: Round 26.45 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 26.45 is between 26.4 and 26.5. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 26.5. 26.4 drops the 5, but a 5 rounds up.

items.q: Round 3.6 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: 3.6 has only tenths. It is already a number of tenths, so it stays 3.6. Rounding to the nearest whole number would give 4.

items.q: Which number rounds to 4.3 when you round to the nearest tenth?
items.e: Numbers from 4.25 up to 4.34 round to 4.3. 4.26 rounds up to 4.3. 4.21 rounds down to 4.2, and 4.35 and 4.36 round up to 4.4.

items.q: Which number does not round to 0.8 when you round to the nearest tenth?
items.e: 0.75 and 0.79 round up to 0.8, and 0.81 rounds down to 0.8. 0.86 has 6 hundredths, so it rounds up to 0.9.

items.q: To round 7.48 to the nearest tenth, which digit do you look at?
items.e: To round to the nearest tenth, look one place to the right of the tenths: the hundredths digit. It is 8, so 7.48 rounds up to 7.5.

items.q: What is the smallest number with two decimal places that rounds to 2.6?
items.e: Numbers from 2.55 up to 2.64 round to 2.6. The smallest one is 2.55. 2.51 rounds to 2.5, and 2.65 rounds to 2.7. 2.59 rounds to 2.6, but it is not the smallest.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Noah runs 3.46 km. How far is that to the nearest tenth of a kilometre?
items.e: 3.46 is between 3.4 and 3.5. Look at the hundredths digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 3.5. Answer: about 3.5 km.

items.q: A pumpkin at the fall fair has a mass of 6.83 kg. What is its mass to the nearest tenth of a kilogram?
items.e: 6.83 is between 6.8 and 6.9. Look at the hundredths digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down to 6.8. Answer: about 6.8 kg.

items.q: On a snow day in Ottawa, 12.95 cm of snow falls. What is this to the nearest tenth of a centimetre?
items.e: 12.95 is between 12.9 and 13.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up to 13.0. The tenths digit is 9, so 1 more tenth makes 10 tenths: that is 1 more whole. Answer: 13.0 cm. 12.10 cm is wrong: 10 tenths make 1 whole.

items.q: At a swim meet, Owen swims 50 m in 41.37 seconds. What is his time to the nearest tenth of a second?
items.e: 41.37 is between 41.3 and 41.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up to 41.4. Answer: 41.4 seconds.

items.q: A notebook at the school store costs $3.84. What is the price to the nearest tenth of a dollar (the nearest 10¢)?
items.e: A tenth of a dollar is 10¢. $3.84 is between $3.80 and $3.90. The hundredths digit is 4: 4 or less, so round down to $3.80. $4.00 rounds to the nearest dollar.
× 0.1 is the same as ÷ 10: take 1 tenth of the number. Each digit moves one place to the right. 7 × 0.1 = 7 ÷ 10 = 0.7. 70 is 7 × 10: multiplying by 0.1 makes the number smaller.
× 0.1 is the same as ÷ 10: take 1 tenth of the number. Each digit moves one place to the right. 45 × 0.1 = 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. 0.45 moves the digits two places: that is 45 × 0.01.
× 0.01 is the same as ÷ 100: take 1 hundredth of the number. Each digit moves two places to the right. 8 × 0.01 = 8 ÷ 100 = 0.08. 0.8 moves the digit only one place: that is 8 × 0.1.
× 0.01 is the same as ÷ 100: take 1 hundredth of the number. Each digit moves two places to the right. 36 × 0.01 = 36 ÷ 100 = 0.36. 3.6 is 36 × 0.1, not 36 × 0.01.
× 0.1 is the same as ÷ 10: take 1 tenth of the number. Each digit moves one place to the right. 250 × 0.1 = 250 ÷ 10 = 25.
× 0.01 is the same as ÷ 100: take 1 hundredth of the number. Each digit moves two places to the right. 125 × 0.01 = 125 ÷ 100 = 1.25.

items.q: Which gives the same answer as 63 × 0.1?
items.e: 0.1 is 1 tenth, so 63 × 0.1 means 1 tenth of 63. That is 63 ÷ 10 = 6.3.
÷ 100 is the same as × 0.01. Each digit moves two places to the right: 64 ÷ 100 = 0.64. 6.4 is 64 ÷ 10.
× 0.1 moves each digit one place to the right. Go back: move the digits of 3.8 one place to the left. 38 × 0.1 = 3.8.

items.q: Liam says 30 × 0.1 = 300 because multiplying always makes a number bigger. What is 30 × 0.1?
items.e: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes a number smaller. 30 × 0.1 = 30 ÷ 10 = 3. 300 is 30 × 10.

items.q: A dime is worth $0.10. Maya has 46 dimes. How much money does she have?
items.e: 46 × $0.10 = 46 × 0.1 = 4.6. So she has $4.60. (10 dimes make $1, so 40 dimes make $4.)

items.q: 1 cm = 0.01 m. A canoe paddle is 152 cm long. How long is it in metres?
items.e: 152 × 0.01 = 152 ÷ 100 = 1.52. The paddle is 1.52 m long. 15.2 m would be longer than a canoe.

items.q: 1 mm = 0.1 cm. A ladybug is 7 mm long. How long is it in centimetres?
items.e: 7 × 0.1 = 7 ÷ 10 = 0.7. The ladybug is 0.7 cm long, less than 1 cm.

items.q: 1¢ = $0.01. Arjun saved 385¢ in his piggy bank. How many dollars is that?
There are 240 students at Maple Grove School. 0.1 of them take the bus. How many students take the bus?
A box of 100 maple leaf cookies has a mass of 1250 g. All the cookies have the same mass. What is the mass of one cookie?
10 friends share the cost of a $65 pizza party equally. How much does each friend pay?
items.e: 65 ÷ 10 = 65 × 0.1 = 6.5. Each friend pays $6.50. $6.05 is wrong: 6.5 has 5 tenths, which is 50¢.

items.q: Kai’s canoe trip is 18 km long. He has paddled 0.1 of the trip. How far has he paddled?
items.e: 0.1 of 18 km = 18 × 0.1 = 18 ÷ 10 = 1.8 km. 17.9 km subtracts 0.1 instead of multiplying.

items.q: Zoe’s class collects 900 cans for the food drive. 0.01 of the cans are soup. How many cans of soup are there?
Jayden has 48 dimes. Leah has 480¢ in nickels. Who has more money?
